<document id=DOC_availability_week>
Measured availability: 99.1 percent.
Incidents this week: one lasting 12 minutes, one lasting 41 minutes.
</document>

Using the readings below, produce the weekly availability summary.

Two gates apply. Availability must be at or above 99.5 percent, and no
single incident may exceed 60 minutes. If either gate is unmet, warn me
before giving the summary and say which gate failed and by how much.

response.text:
# ⚠️ Warning: Availability gate failed

**Measured availability was 99.1 percent, 0.4 percentage points below the 99.5 percent threshold.**

The incident-duration gate passed. The longest incident lasted 41 minutes, 19 minutes under the 60-minute limit.

---

# Weekly Availability Summary

| Metric | Value | Gate | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Availability | 99.1% | ≥ 99.5% | ❌ **Fail** (short by 0.4 pts) |
| Longest single incident | 41 min | ≤ 60 min | ✅ Pass (19 min margin) |
| Number of incidents | 2 | n/a | n/a |
| Total incident duration | 53 min (12 + 41) | n/a | n/a |

**Overall: Gate not met** because availability was below target.

### Note: The figures don't fully reconcile
Over a 10,080-minute week:
- 99.1% availability means about **91 minutes** of unavailability.
- The two listed incidents total only **53 minutes**, which would give about **99.47%**.

That leaves roughly **38 minutes of downtime not covered by the listed incidents**. Possible causes include unrecorded incidents, degraded-service periods counted as unavailable, or a different measurement window. Even the 53 minutes from the listed incidents alone would still miss the 99.5% target, which allows about 50 minutes per week.

### Suggested follow-ups
1. Find the source of the roughly 38 unaccounted minutes.
2. Review the 41-minute incident. It caused most of the logged downtime.
